PE-50 catheter preparation for the carotid artery catheterization. (A) A 12-inch piece of PE-50 catheter with Vannas spring scissors and a 25 G needle, (B) Insert the 25 G needle into any end of the PE-50 catheter, (C) Zoomed-in view of the other end of the PE-50 catheter cut at 45° angle with Vannas spring scissors. Preparation of umbilical venous catheter (UVC) for RHC Bend 3.3 cm of 16 G beveled needle to a curve at a 65° angle ( Figure 4A ). Note: The main pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle and curves posteriorly and slightly to the left before branching into the left and right pulmonary arteries. The 65° angle bending of the needle and the catheter mimics the curved pulmonary artery. Insert 2.8 cm of the 3.5 French single lumen polyurethane UVC into the curved needle ( Figure 4B ). Note: Proper orientation of the curved needle during catheterization is of utmost importance, with the number markings on the UVC being required to face upwards during insertion of the needle. Furthermore, during insertion of the catheter into the right jugular vein, the orientation will ensure that the curvature of the catheter is parallel to the number markings, permitting the surgeon to determine the insertion length of the UVC. Submerge the UVC containing the bent needle in 45 °C deionized water for 2 min. After 2 min, remove the UVC containing the bent needle from the 45 °C deionized water and place it in room temperature deionized water immediately. Remove the catheter from the needle; upon taking it out from cold water, the shape of the UVC should conform to the shape of the bent needle ( Figure 4C ). Note: To reuse the curved UVC, keep the curved needle inserted inside the curved catheter to maintain the curvature, as shown in Figure 4B . It is critical to ensure the curved catheter retains the 65° to avoid missing the pulmonary artery during insertion, which can lead to reinsertions and the eventual puncturing of the artery. Figure

steps.title: Prepare PE‑50 catheter for carotid
steps.instruction: Cut a 12‑inch piece of PE‑50 tubing with Vannas spring scissors; insert a beveled 1‑inch 25 G needle into one end so the needle fits snugly inside the tubing without perforation; cut the opposite end of the tubing at a 45° angle with Vannas spring scissors to create a slanted tip for insertion into the right carotid artery.

steps.title: Prepare curved UVC for right heart
steps.instruction: Bend 3.3 cm of a 16 G beveled needle to a 65° angle; insert 2.8 cm of the 3.5 Fr single‑lumen polyurethane umbilical vessel catheter (UVC) into the curved needle ensuring the catheter’s numeric markings face upward; submerge the needle‑UVC assembly in 45 °C de‑ionized water for 2 min, then transfer immediately to room‑temperature de‑ionized water; remove the needle, leaving the UVC curved to 65°.

steps.title: Assemble steel‑suture guide wire (optional)
steps.instruction: Attach a 3‑way stopcock to a pressure transducer; connect the 3.5 Fr dual‑lumen silicone UVC to the stopcock; thread a surgical stainless‑steel suture through the UVC up to the catheter tip and tighten the stopcock knob so the suture is fully inserted but protrudes only from the knob, hanging as excess wire.

steps.title: Prepare catheter sleeve (optional)
steps.instruction: Open the Safelet IV 20 G 1" Luer‑tapered catheter sleeve; detach and discard the needle; cut off the syringe fitting from the top and trim the sleeve tip; insert the single‑lumen polyurethane UVC into the sleeve until the catheter tip aligns with the sleeve tip.

steps.title: Set up PowerLab and transducers
steps.instruction: Connect the PowerLab to a computer via USB and to power; attach two bridge amplifiers (one for mPAP, one for mSAP) to the PowerLab; connect each amplifier output to the PowerLab input and to an MLT1199 SP844 kit; affix the bottom of each pressure transducer sensor to a 6 in × 6 in acrylic sheet with hot‑glue; label each amplifier and its cables with the corresponding PowerLab port number.

steps.title: Assemble saline calibration manifold
steps.instruction: Attach a red 3‑way stopcock (female Luer) to the male swivel Luer lock of a disposable clip‑on dome; attach a blue 3‑way stopcock (male swivel) to the opposite side of the dome; orient the red knob to block flow to the left outlet (forcing flow toward the blue stopcock) and the blue knob to allow flow in all directions except upward.

steps.title: Prime dome with saline
steps.instruction: Fill a 1 mL HSW syringe with 0.9 % (w/v) isotonic saline and insert it into the inlet of the red stopcock; depress the plunger until saline exits the right outlet of the blue stopcock, then turn the red knob to restrict flow in all directions; remove the syringe, refill with saline, place it in the blue stopcock inlet, turn the blue knob to block flow toward the dome, and depress until saline exits the right outlet; leave the syringe in the blue inlet; repeat with a second syringe in the red inlet, turning the red knob to allow flow everywhere except toward the dome and depress until saline exits the left outlet; finally, insert the dome onto a transducer sensor and set the blue knob to allow flow in all directions except upward, establishing 0 mmHg (atmospheric) pressure in the dome.

steps.title: Two‑point calibration in LabChart
steps.instruction: Turn on PowerLab and open LabChart Pro; connect the Delta‑Cal pressure transducer male swivel to the blue stopcock female port; verify the reading is 0 mmHg; start continuous acquisition, right‑click the channel, select Bridge Amp, then Zero; keep the red knob restricting upward/left flow and the blue knob restricting all flow; in LabChart, set channel scale to 100:1 or 200:1, auto‑scale the Y‑axis, and select the region covering the entire trace; turn the Delta‑Cal knob clockwise to 50 mmHg, add a comment “50”, record at least 3 s of data; increase to 120 mmHg, add comment “120”, record at least 3 s; stop acquisition; select the 50 mmHg region, click the arrow next to Point 1, average the values and type 50; repeat for Point 2 with the 120 mmHg region; set units to mmHg and confirm the conversion; verify calibration by setting Delta‑Cal to 80 mmHg and confirming the display (±1 mmHg acceptable).

steps.title: Pre‑operative animal preparation
steps.instruction: Clean all surgical tools with soap, water, then 70 % isopropyl alcohol; place a heating pad under an inverted light microscope, clean the pad surface with 70 % isopropyl alcohol, turn on the pad and set to 37 °C (maintain throughout); place Sprague‑Dawley rats in an induction chamber with 2.5 % isoflurane; once anesthetized, inject intraperitoneally 300 µL per 250 g body weight of a cocktail containing 1 mL of 100 mg/mL ketamine and 100 µL of 20 mg/mL xylazine; confirm depth of anesthesia with toe‑pinch, administering supplemental doses as needed; position the rat supine on the heating pad, restrain all four limbs with 3 M Micropore tape and secure the head with a string under the upper incisors; optionally trim hair from ventral neck and dorsal scapular area, then scrub three times with Betadine® followed by 70 % isopropyl alcohol.

steps.title: Expose left carotid artery
steps.instruction: Using straight Mayo scissors, make a ~3 cm midline skin incision on the ventral neck and blunt‑dissect the skin from subcutaneous tissue; with tenotomy scissors, cut connective tissue and muscle lateral to the trachea; separate muscle layers deeper until the left carotid artery and its accompanying nerve are visible; gently separate the nerve from the artery with curved‑tip Graefe forceps.

steps.title: Catheterize left carotid artery
steps.instruction: Place a Graefe forceps under the artery to lift it; tie a 5‑0 silk suture around the arterial segment toward the head with a double knot followed by a single knot to stop cranial blood flow; place a micro‑serrefine on the distal (heart‑ward) end if the artery is throbbing; leave an open double knot on the distal end (before the serrefine); using a micro‑dissecting spring scissor, make a ~0.5 mm hole in the artery (slightly larger than the catheter tip); grasp the prepared PE‑50 catheter with angled vessel cannulation forceps and insert 1.0 cm of the catheter through the hole; secure the catheter with a piece of Micropore tape; close the open double knot and add a single knot over the catheter; tie an additional double‑then‑single knot with the first suture to anchor the catheter; remove the micro‑serrefine; confirm arterial pressure waveforms on the computer; flush the catheter with saline using a pre‑filled syringe; tape the external catheter to the heating pad; cover the exposed tracheal area with gauze pads secured with Micropore tape; after data collection, flush the catheter with 99 % isopropyl alcohol (reuse only if unpunctured and clear).

steps.title: Expose right jugular vein
steps.instruction: Using tenotomy scissors for coarse cuts and spring scissors for fine cuts, separate the muscle layers on the far‑right side of the trachea near the scapula to locate the bifurcation of the right jugular vein; place a Graefe forceps under the vein below the bifurcation to lift it and keep it exposed.

steps.title: Prepare right jugular for catheterization
steps.instruction: Tie a 5‑0 silk suture around the jugular segment toward the head (below the bifurcation) with a double knot then a single knot to stop cranial flow; leave an open double knot on the distal (heart‑ward) end; make a ~0.5 mm incision in the vein with a micro‑dissecting spring scissor at the larger lumen region.

steps.title: Insert catheter using guide wire (method A)
steps.instruction: If using the steel‑suture guide wire, adjust the transducer setup as described in the guide‑wire section; thread the UVC with the steel suture through the angled vessel cannulation forceps; hold the jugular incision with a Graefe forceps; slowly advance the catheter 6 cm (rat < 250 g) or 8 cm (rat > 250 g) toward the heart, maintaining the orientation shown in Figure 15F; once the catheter tip reaches the pulmonary artery, pull the steel suture outward to allow the curved catheter to resume its 65° shape; confirm pulmonary artery pressure waveform; secure the catheter with Micropore tape and close the open double knot with a single knot; cover the right side with gauze pads secured with tape.

steps.title: Insert catheter using sleeve (method B)
steps.instruction: Grab the bent UVC together with the catheter sleeve using angled vessel cannulation forceps; insert 1 cm of the sleeve into the jugular vein while keeping the numeric markings facing upward; then advance the catheter 6–8 cm toward the heart; while holding the catheter stationary, pull the sleeve back, leaving only the UVC inside the vein; advance the UVC tip until pulmonary artery pressure waveform appears; secure as above with tape and knot; cover with gauze.

steps.title: Insert catheter without guide (method C)
steps.instruction: Hold the curved UVC with hollowed angled vessel cannulation forceps; use extra‑fine Graefe forceps to stabilize the jugular incision; carefully advance the catheter 6–8 cm toward the heart, allowing the tip to assume its 65° curvature as it progresses; monitor pressure waveforms to identify right atrium (2–6 mmHg), right ventricle (0–25 mmHg), and pulmonary artery (10–25 mmHg) peaks; once pulmonary artery waveform is confirmed, secure the catheter with Micropore tape and close the open double knot with a single knot; cover the right side with gauze pads.

steps.title: Pre‑fill catheters and begin measurements
steps.instruction: Attach the PE‑50 catheter (carotid) and the UVC (pulmonary) to the red stopcock male ports; set the red knob to allow flow left and right but block upward, and set the blue knob to block all flow (Figure 12A); press the saline‑filled syringe to pre‑fill both catheters; then rotate the knobs to the measurement orientation (red knob blocks upward flow, blue knob blocks all flow) as shown in Figure 12B; insert the free ends of the catheters into the respective transducer domes; start simultaneous data acquisition of mSAP and mPAP on LabChart.

steps.title: Terminate experiment and clean
steps.instruction: After the required recording period (≥ 6 h), euthanize the rat by injecting isopropyl alcohol through the transducer domes until a flat line is observed; flush both catheters with 99 % isopropyl alcohol using a syringe; store catheters for reuse only if they remain unpunctured and transparent; dispose of all animal waste according to institutional biosafety guidelines.
